thesis: Lam Research is the memory-capex pure play among big semicap names: record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5.84B (+24% y/y) with EPS +41%, June-quarter guidance of $6.6B, a raised $140B calendar-2026 WFE outlook, and the first $2.1B quarter for its services business. The memory supercycle (see MU's 85% gross margins) guarantees near-term tool demand - and explains why LRCX fell ~14% this week alongside Micron: the market is starting to price the other side of the memory mountain. At ~53x forward EPS, the stock carries compounder multiples into the most cyclical corner of semicap.
catalysts: Q4 FY2026 results (~late July 2026): guidance $6.6B +/- 0.4B revenue, GM 50.5%, EPS 1.65 +/- 0.15
Calendar-2026 WFE outlook already raised to $140B (from $135B); H2 > H1 expected
Memory-fab capacity announcements from Micron/Samsung/SK hynix (direct order flow to Lam)
Customer Support Business Group momentum (record $2.1B quarter - recurring-revenue mix shift)
Advanced packaging and gate-all-around etch/deposition share gains
risk_factors: Memory concentration: Lam's etch/deposition leadership skews to NAND/DRAM - the segment whose 85% margins today guarantee a supply response and capex digestion later
Valuation: ~53x forward EPS (guide ~6.60/yr run-rate) vs a historical semicap band of 15-25x
The -13.87% week tracking Micron's -14.94% shows the stock trades as a memory derivative in drawdowns (beta 1.80)
China/export-control exposure common to all semicap (peer AMAT just paid a $253M settlement)
WFE outlooks are revised down as fast as up when memory prices turn
